description: Spec-Driven Development traceability registry. Each requirement links a PsyUML spec section (the source of truth) to a roadmap milestone and the implementation/test paths that will satisfy it. Validated by sdd/check.mjs. Statuses: planned | in-progress | implemented | deprecated. "implemented" means the in-repo deliverable (code/docs/tests) for the requirement is complete and green; it does NOT assert clinical validation. Real-world clinical evidence (layperson comprehension, inter-rater reliability, multi-school consensus) is the Stage-4 v1.0 gate, tracked solely by REQ-EVAL-SUITE, which stays in-progress until those human studies run. PsyUML remains an unvalidated v0.x design. Impl/test paths are existence-checked only once a requirement leaves 'planned'.

milestones.title: v0.2: diagram families + audience profiles foundation
v0.2: lossy FHIR export + audience-scoped exports

requirements.title: 8-category core ontology + metamodel (OT/RT/PT)
requirements.notes: Nodes (8 element categories), typed connectors, and the property bag. Stereotypes per §K.

requirements.title: Concrete notation: glyphs + connectors render to SVG
requirements.notes: Native SVG authoritative; Mermaid is approximate export only. The editor authors the typed connector set (§C) directly: a Links panel adds/labels/removes edges of any kind (sequential/exit/containment/reciprocal/transference/…) between nodes — no DSL required (e2e-covered). Layout legibility is now machine-checked: a shared geometry layer (packages/render/layout.ts: one textWidth metric + the separate1D VPSC/Fast-Node-Overlap-Removal core) plus data-el element tagging let packages/render/overlap.test.ts assert, over the whole corpus + generated stress models, that node boxes, node labels, and (for most renderers) edge labels never overlap and stay in-frame — under the shared text-metric model (ADR-0012).

requirements.title: State Map diagram type
Parts/Agents Map diagram type
GUI editor: palette, properties panel, save/load, export
requirements.notes: M2: example-keyed picker over 12 diagram types; live render with layer/monochrome/school toggles. Structured authoring closes the gaps a build-a-diagram agent test found: an add-node form makes a node of any kind/stereotype (was: add-only on 2 types, generic only); a Links panel connects two nodes with a typed, labelled edge and removes edges (was: NO way to author relationships in the GUI — the unanimous #1 gap); node panel does rename / mark certainty / hide / remove; Diagram-details editor sets title/disclaimer/crisis. Plus save/load .psyuml, SVG export, Text (DSL) view/edit (Apply step clarified after agents read it as read-only), version snapshots + compare/diff. A Playwright onboarding journey drives it end-to-end, including building a link in the GUI. A second (Playwright) usability eval closed the next round of gaps: the Title is surfaced (was buried in a collapsed panel); New (blank) + Open .psyuml (resume saved work; Save had no counterpart) added; Save/Export show the blocking reason ON the disabled button (was only in the health panel); download filenames come from the title (were the diagram id, risking overwrite); the add-node form + a per-node 'more' disclosure now author the plain-language client label, the stereotype (with per-diagram hints so a decision diamond = stereotype 'question' is discoverable), and provenance — so realistic authoring no longer forces the DSL; the Links panel speaks friendly connector names and offers a ⚑ trigger; and monochrome is now passed to every renderer (the toggle was a no-op for most types). A new validate notice (render.node-not-shown, info) surfaces a node a diagram won't draw instead of silently dropping it. View controls (zoom / fit / pan-by-scroll) let a user enlarge and read a dense diagram (complementing the scalable layout fix, ADR-0010). Drag-to-reposition is now wired for hand-laid-out diagrams (genogram / relational field): the renderer tags each node with a data-node-id hook, the editor maps the pointer to SVG user space via getScreenCTM and persists node.position (setNodePosition; round-trips as pos=x,y); other diagram types are auto-laid-out and ignore drag. A second usability eval (ADR-0011) added an unsaved-changes confirm before a sample switch / New / Open discards edits (a dirty flag comparing the current vs. last-loaded model), synced the diagram selector after Open, and surfaced edges a diagram won't draw (render.edge-not-shown).

requirements.title: UX research → per-persona user stories + cross-cutting requirements
requirements.notes: Deep-research synthesis (5 angles, primary-source-verified): 5 personas (therapist/client/solo/researcher/ritual), MoSCoW requirements (accessibility WCAG 2.2, plain-language client layer, colour-redundant, crisis-for-constriction, local-first privacy, co-authorship, emotional safety, no-diagnosis), risks/anti-requirements, and the usability-test open questions feeding REQ-EVAL-SUITE. Editor implemented; a Playwright onboarding journey (e2e/onboarding.spec.ts) drives the partially-understood-situation flow through the browser: safety posture visible, co-authorship relabel, progressive-reveal hide (reversible), snapshot (save-incomplete) + diff, and the acute-risk escalation banner. ADR-0013: the editor now wears a hand-rolled, token-based design system (apps/web/styles.css, no UI framework) — an Okabe–Ito-grounded palette shared with the diagrams, a calm/professional card surface, a mobile-first + responsive layout (no horizontal overflow at ~360px, richer multi-column at min-width breakpoints, >=44px touch targets), and colour shown by default in the editor (initial monochrome toggle off; toggle kept as the print path) while colour stays redundant; App.tsx moved from inline styles to semantic className's with every aria-label/role/region/button/summary hook preserved byte-identical (the 8 e2e tests stay green). The site also ships proper web metadata: favicons + apple-touch + PWA web-app manifest (any-maskable icons), a 1200×630 Open Graph/Twitter card, theme-color (light+dark) and a description — all generated from one on-brand SVG mark by scripts/gen-icons.mjs (rasterized via Playwright; committed under apps/web/public/).

requirements.title: Collaborative co-authorship + client ownership of the formulation
requirements.notes: UX-M6 / P1.1 / P2.2: shared/concurrent editing, free-text + verbatim labels, visible authorship, client can relabel/hide/correct, reversible. Collaboration is the evidence-supported active ingredient (Thrower 2024; BPS 2011). M2: in-place per-layer label editing, per-node remove (removeNode cascades incident edges), hide/reveal (reversible), and certainty marking — all reversible via an earlier snapshot. Real-time concurrent editing is later.

requirements.title: Emotional-safety UX: progressive reveal, save-incomplete, non-pathologizing defaults
requirements.notes: UX-M7 / P1.3 / P2.3: a poorly-handled formulation can distress (Redhead 2015) — progressive reveal, never force completion, soft wording, opt-in trauma detail, no unprompted 'verdict' diagram. M2: per-node hide/show (progressive reveal) via the node panel + standing disclaimer + save-incomplete (nothing auto-finalized) shipped.

requirements.title: Decision/Navigation (crisis) chart, client-usable
requirements.notes: UX-M4 (crisis-for-cognitive-constriction): one decision/step, escalation ladder, localized crisis resources on every screen, means-restriction step, no dead-ends, human escalation, large text (Stanley 2018; Morrison 2024). No AI handles crises. M2: renderDecisionChart + always-visible crisis banner + decision-nav example shipped; the no-dead-ends / crisis-resource-present lint lands in M3 (REQ-SAFETY-TRIAGE). Crisis line now renders ON the crisis node (wrapped), not only in the always-visible bottom banner (pilot comprehension fix); and it is region-neutral — points to 'your local number' rather than a single country's line (ADR-0008, de-US-centering the pilot flagged). The layout is now scalable and cycle-aware (ADR-0010): a plan that loops back ('still not safe → go back to the crisis step') no longer collapses the cycle and everything below it onto one overlapping row — back-edges are classified by DFS and the forward edges are longest-path layered, the canvas grows to fit the widest layer with a content-fit viewBox, and branch labels are offset/wrapped so they don't overprint; the on-screen/JSON disclaimer is now also rendered into the exported SVG (was omitted). Round 2 (ADR-0011): node labels are wrapped INSIDE their box (diamonds narrower) so a long clinical step no longer overflows and collides with its sibling.

requirements.title: Resource/Anchor map
requirements.notes: M2: renderResourceMap (categorized anchors under People/Skills/Values/Soothing, CFT footer) + resource-anchor example shipped and wired into the editor.

requirements.title: Process/Loop diagram type (maintaining cycles)
requirements.notes: renderLoopMap (ring layout, reciprocal double-headed links, reinforcing/balancing centre badge, dashed exits) + process-loop example, wired into the editor; path-of-hope validation applies (a loop must show a way out). Ring layout now orders nodes in cycle order (follow the sequential chain) so steps are adjacent and edges stop crossing the middle — only the closing edge spans (pilot legibility fix).

requirements.title: Abstract-syntax well-formedness rules enforced
requirements.notes: Enforced: single-source/target edges + live endpoints (r2), band refs resolve (r1), relations join people/parts/contexts not states/resources (r3), interventions never float unattached (r4), dissociative barriers separate only parts/states (r6), client-facing disclaimer + crisis-resource gate (r7). r5 loop typing is structural (loop marker is the R/B enum); full closed-path/exit detection tracked with the diff/loop work.

requirements.title: No meaning by color alone; monochrome-printable; min text size; alt-text + text summary per view
requirements.notes: Every rendered view also emits a plain-language text summary + alt text (Source 3 C8, WCAG 2.2). The editor itself meets WCAG 2.2 AA — keyboard operation, contrast, 200% zoom, target size, colour-redundant (UX-M1, docs/ux). M3: validate flags over-long labels (a11y.label-length); the examples corpus is lint-gated in CI. Conformance asserts, per view + both layers, role=img + aria-label + non-empty alt text and monochrome-by-default (no colour hue). Render legibility hardened (ADR-0006) after a build-a-diagram agent test: content-fit viewBoxes (renderLoopMap, incl. negative coords + honor pos), node-center clamping (state map), a fitText helper (single-line compress) and a wrapLabel helper (true multi-line tspan wrapping) adopted across the box/shape renderers (state, loop, parts, mode, relational/genogram, intervention-sequence, two-triangles) — so labels never clip or overflow on screen or in exports. Cross-school disagreement is carried in the text channel too: the Parts Map alt-text names any element claimed by >1 school ('Origins disagree on: … — both claims are shown, not merged', ADR-0007). Non-overlap is now a machine-checked invariant (ADR-0012): renderers size slots to a shared textWidth metric, spread siblings with separate1D (VPSC / Fast Node Overlap Removal), and grow the canvas rather than overlap; packages/render/overlap.test.ts proves no node↔node / label↔non-owner-node overlap and full in-frame containment across the corpus + stress models (label↔label too for ten of twelve renderers; documented known-gap for parts-map + process-loop) — holding under the shared text-metric model; edge line/path crossings are out of scope. ADR-0013: the editor's chrome is now a hand-rolled, token-based design system (apps/web/styles.css) carrying that WCAG 2.2 AA posture explicitly — an Okabe–Ito-grounded palette with darker -strong text/border variants for >=4.5:1 (text) / >=3:1 (UI/large) contrast, a visible focus ring, a mobile-first + responsive layout with no horizontal overflow at ~360px and >=44px touch targets (verified by Playwright screenshots at 390x844 / 1280x800 + a programmatic overflow + target-size audit), prefers-color-scheme dark + prefers-reduced-motion support, and colour-by-default in the editor that stays redundant (state cues keep their text + glyph); the render layer keeps its monochrome-by-default default (conformance unchanged).

requirements.title: Path-of-hope clinical-safety lint (no hopeless-only diagrams)
requirements.notes: Generalizes §A.2-r5 to every diagram; hard-block in the client layer. Companion-paper idea A4. M3: implemented in @psyuml/validate (warn for clinician, error for client) + surfaced in the editor's formulation-health panel, gating export.

requirements.title: Disclaimer + crisis fields gating; non-pathologizing client layer
requirements.notes: M3: client-facing diagrams require a standing disclaimer (error if missing); the editor gates export on a clean validation report. Standing non-diagnosis + 'Unvalidated v0.x' note shown in the editor. ADR-0005 records the client-facing classification (process-loop added; two-triangles excluded as a clinician aid). The editor's Diagram-details panel (editor.ts setMeta) lets a user add the title/disclaimer/crisis line in-UI, so a client diagram can be un-blocked for export instead of hitting an unfixable gate.

requirements.title: School profiles + polymorphic re-render + translation table
requirements.notes: One immutable model, many views. M4: @psyuml/profiles ships the §G.2 parts-family translation table (TRANSLATIONS) + translate() + roleLabelsFor(); the renderer takes a roleLabels map and the editor's School switcher (IFS/schema/structural-dissociation/TA) re-labels the Parts Map vocabulary while keeping structure. SCOPE (sharpened after the simulated Tier-B pilot, ADR-adjacent honesty fix): the vocabulary swap is the parts family ONLY; CAT is deliberately excluded (reciprocal roles are dyadic, not a parts slot); other traditions (polyvagal, CAT/SDR, genogram, Malan, Karpman, ritual) are their own diagram types — a CBT loop vs a CAT reformulation are different formulations, NOT one model relabelled. Opposed-claim surfacing (ADR-0007, from the pilot's CAT critique): @psyuml/model exports schoolClaims() (school-agnostic; reads bare AND school: tags) so validate fires on real corpus data — provenance.node-mixed-school (per element) + provenance.mixed-school (per diagram), both info — and the Parts Map now RENDERS a node claimed by >1 school as a contested-origin marker (⚖ A vs B), naming the conflict in alt-text too (§D). Deferred (enhancements beyond this requirement, not blockers): contested rendering on other diagram types (Parts Map only today), explaining HOW two claims disagree (not just naming the schools), and full per-diagram profiles + more swap families.

requirements.title: Relational Field / genogram (McGoldrick–Gerson–Petry set) — diagram type §E.3
requirements.notes: renderRelationalField: manual node positions; gender glyphs (male square / female circle / other diamond / system dashed); index double-border; McGoldrick relation line styles (close solid, distant dashed, conflict zigzag, fused triple, cutoff slashed) + nestedWithin origin thread (fine-dotted + ring) + ecomap. Subsumes the drama triangle (§E.3) — see drama-triangle.psyuml under REQ-RESEARCH-PROFILES. Completes the 9-type diagram catalog. Cross-school re-render/translation table still under REQ-CROSS-SCHOOL.

requirements.title: Profiles & stereotypes extension mechanism
requirements.notes: §K implemented as a typed, VALIDATED profile registry in @psyuml/profiles (ADR-0009), per the 'validation first' directive. ExtensionProfile/StereotypeDef (zod) + validateProfile enforce the four §K rules — rule 1 base specializes a core element (CORE_BASES = model NodeKind∪EdgeKind, so it can't drift from the model), rule 2 Tier-1 is frozen (extensions default Tier 3), rule 3 a complete compat matrix per DiagramType + glyph/hand/non-color/≥1-synonym kit, rule 4 no collision with a reserved Tier-1 glyph (CORE_TIER1_GLYPHS from §B/§C, incl. ⚖) — plus unique ids, a semver warning, and a deprecation-info note; malformed input returns profile.shape issues rather than throwing. roleLabelsFromProfile feeds the renderer's roleLabels; CFT_PROFILE is a shipped worked example. Surfaces: `psyuml lint-profile <file>` (CLI) + conformance §K invariants. Deferred (enhancements beyond this requirement, not blockers): live profile loading in the editor's School switcher (beyond roleLabelsFromProfile); auto-verifying the author-asserted compat matrix against each renderer; per-diagram-type custom-stereotype rendering.

requirements.title: Schema Mode Map, CAT SDR, Malan Two Triangles, Karpman nested triangles
requirements.notes: Companion-paper profiles; each per §K extension rules (idea-incorporation §2). M5: Schema Mode Map shipped (renderModeMap — circle size = dominance with redundant numeral, §D; Healthy-Adult growth target; vulnerable-child wound marker). Karpman drama triangle shipped as a Relational Field instance (spec §E.3): drama-triangle.psyuml places Persecutor/Rescuer/Victim with a NESTED historical triangle wired via the nestedWithin connector (drawn by relLine as a fine-dotted origin thread with a ring). Malan Two Triangles shipped as the two-triangles diagram type (renderTwoTriangles): the Triangle of Conflict (Defence/Anxiety/Hidden feeling) + Triangle of Person (Current/Transference/Past) as band-grouped triads linked by the transference connector (dotted) — closing the last dangling edge kind. Both nestedWithin and transference are now used. CAT SDR shipped as a process-loop instance (cat-sdr.psyuml): the reciprocal role (criticizing ⇄ criticized) via the reciprocal double-arrow, the trap procedure as edge labels, marked exits, and the CAT observing-eye glyph (renderLoopMap now draws an eye for stereotype 'observing-eye'). All four named M5 research profiles (Schema Mode Map, Karpman, Malan, CAT SDR) are shipped; the §K mechanism stays open for further profiles.

requirements.title: Model versioning + diff view (longitudinal progress)
requirements.notes: Companion-paper idea A6. Versions documents, not the person. M6: @psyuml/diff ships diffModels() — matches nodes/edges by stable id (§H.10) so a rename reads as a label change, surfaces the spec's progress deltas (dominance up/down, forming/liminal->consolidated 'dashed->solid', valence, add/remove/rename) — plus summarizeDiff() readable lines and isEmptyDiff(). render.renderDiff() draws an accessible monochrome 'progress card' (↑/↓ glyphs + a dashed->solid swatch, §D); the editor has a 'Compare with...' file load showing the changes-since panel + an Export-progress-SVG button, plus in-session version snapshots (snapshotModel/restoreVersion in editor.ts: Snapshot button → an immutable serialized snapshot list with per-version Compare/Restore). Deferred (enhancements beyond this requirement, not blockers): persisting versions across reloads (localStorage) and Timeline/Trajectory (§E.5) wiring.

requirements.title: Timeline/Trajectory diagram type
requirements.notes: renderTimeline: bands = time columns, stereotype action/identity = the two narrative landscapes, with a problem-saturated -> preferred-future baseline + trajectory arrows. timeline example wired into the editor.

requirements.title: Intervention Sequence diagram type
requirements.notes: renderInterventionSeq: actor swimlanes (bands) as columns, interventions as hexagons placed by longest-path phase order, guards as edge labels; example wired into the editor. The grief-ritual interop node (§F.6) lands with the Ritual diagram (M7).

requirements.title: Ritual modality first-class, secular variant + honest framing required
requirements.notes: renderRitual (van Gennep phase columns, LIMINAL dashed, ritual-act hexagons, mandatory framing+secular footer); model.meta.ritual carries framing/secularVariant; validate errors if either is missing (ethics.ritual-framing / ethics.ritual-secular), so the editor blocks ritual export without them. §F.6 interop (same hexagon as an Intervention-Sequence node) follows.

requirements.title: Bounded narrative→draft-model assist (human-in-the-loop, formulation-only)
requirements.notes: No diagnosis/severity scoring; no safeguard-bypass. M8: @psyuml/ai ships assist(narrative,{model,consented,terms},extractor?) — the GUARDRAILS of the Source-3 pipeline, enforced + tested with no live model call: consent gate (no consent -> nothing processed); PII minimization via @psyuml/privacy.redactText BEFORE the extractor sees the text; safety triage that HALTS and escalates before extraction (when requiresHumanEscalation(model) or a coarse acute-risk/psychosis marker trips); every suggestion wrapped low-confidence (confidence 'L', epistemicStatus 'inferred'); nothing auto-applied (applySuggestions is a separate explicit accept step). The narrative->suggestions step is a pluggable Extractor (default noopExtractor) so a model-agnostic LLM extractor drops in without changing the safety envelope, and the package is isolated (removing it leaves the editor working). Deferred/optional: an actual LLM-backed extractor is a pluggable plug-in the project owner shelved (the safety envelope + no-op seam are complete and tested); an in-editor AI panel is a UI enhancement. The de-identification audit trail ships in @psyuml/privacy (redactionAudit).

requirements.title: Text DSL ⇄ model round-trip + CLI
requirements.notes: M9: @psyuml/grammar ships toDSL()/fromDSL() — a line-oriented text surface (diagram/lang/title/disclaimer/crisis/ritual/flag headers; band/node/edge statements; double-quoted free text with \" + \\ escapes; omit-on-default + a labeljson escape for multi-language labels). Lossless round-trip is proven over the whole corpus (fromDSL(toDSL(parseModel(x))) deep-equals parseModel(x)) since both sides are parseModel-normalized; the editor has a Text (DSL) view/edit panel. @psyuml/cli ships `psyuml lint|render|convert` as a pure run(argv,io) (unit-tested with a fake IO) bundled to a runnable dist/cli/psyuml.mjs by scripts/build-cli.mjs (esbuild, already in the toolchain): lint validates JSON-or-DSL input (auto-detected) and exits non-zero on any error-severity issue — a CI/pre-commit gate mirroring the editor's export gate. Deferred (enhancements beyond this requirement, not blockers): a FHIR/SNOMED `export` subcommand (REQ-INTEROP-FHIR) and non-programmer-friendly parse error messages (idea-incorporation §7).

requirements.title: Conformance suite + semver release flow (v1.0 readiness)
requirements.notes: Leaving v0.x stays gated on the spec's Stage-4 clinical evidence. Conformance includes the round-trip invariant (Source 3). M10: conformance/ suite runs per-example round-trip + validation (both layers) + accessible-SVG (role/aria/alt) + monochrome + type coverage, in CI.

requirements.title: Epistemic status on every node/edge (reported/observed/inferred/planned/symbolic)
requirements.notes: Source 3 C2. Formulation as working hypothesis. Rendered via a redundant, collision-checked line-style + tag; never system-confirmed for ritual/spiritual claims. Editor: a per-node 'certainty' control (editor.ts setNodeEpistemic) lets a user mark a node reported/observed/inferred(a guess)/planned/etc. — the core move for diagramming an only-partially-understood situation (covered by the Playwright onboarding journey).

requirements.title: Multilingual model: stable concept IDs separate from localized labels (BCP 47, Unicode)
requirements.notes: Source 3 C7. label = { BCP-47 -> text } over a stable id; clinician/client variants per language.

requirements.title: Clinical-hazard lint + risk/psychosis safety gate
requirements.notes: Source 3 C3. Acute-risk/psychosis -> block autonomous formulation + human-review banner; risky-ritual materials -> documentation-only; typed-edge requirement; mixed-school provenance; PII redact-by-default. Gates the AI-assist pipeline. M3: crisis no-dead-ends + crisis-resources lint shipped; acute-risk + psychosis triage now act on meta.safety (escalation warning, acute-risk-requires-crisis-resources error, ritual-under-psychosis contraindication) + a mixed-school provenance notice; validate exports requiresHumanEscalation() which the editor reads to raise a clinical-escalation banner and which AI-assist (M8) reads to halt. Crisis resources stay region-neutral by design (ADR-0008: no per-country numbers baked in — a wrong number is a hazard); safety.crisis-localize (info) nudges a concrete local contact (number/URL/handle) when acute risk is flagged but the line names none. Typed edges are enforced at parse time (EdgeKind required). PII redact-by-default still lands with privacy/AI (M8).

requirements.title: Body Map view (somatic: body-located sensations, arousal curve, sensory channels)
requirements.notes: Source 3 C4. renderBodyMap: body silhouette + sensations placed by position, sized by intensity (redundant numeral, §D), with a pacing/titration safety note. body-map example wired into the editor. Arousal-curve / sensory-channel overlays can follow.

requirements.title: Privacy-by-default: de-identification, role-scoped export, redaction, audit log, consent
requirements.notes: Source 3 C10 (HIPAA/GDPR-informed). Local-first; no PHI leaves device without role-specific consent; conservative human-supervised-formulation posture, not live-care CDS. M8: @psyuml/privacy ships deidentify(model,{terms}) — scrubs node/edge/band/trigger labels + title (emails, links, phone-like runs, caller-supplied name terms) and reports each redaction, while preserving the public-safe disclaimer + crisis line; never mutates input. Exposed as `psyuml redact` (writes de-identified JSON, prints the count to stderr). This is the PII-minimization step for AI-assist (M8) and the basis for a de-identified interop export (M9). Hardened after a cold-eyes test: name terms match via (?<!\w)..(?!\w) lookarounds rather than \b, so a term ending in a non-word char (e.g. the initials 'R.') is actually redacted — previously it silently matched nothing; the CLI also warns when a --term matches nothing.  Implemented: de-identification (deidentify/redactText), role-scoped export (scopeToLayer — client never leaks clinician wording, drops hidden nodes), an audit trail (redactionAudit + CLI), and consent as a first-class meta.consent field gated in the AI pipeline and at the CLI client-share step.

requirements.title: FHIR/SNOMED + de-identified research export
requirements.notes: Source 3 C6, re-opened by the v0.2 research synthesis and specced concretely in v0.2 §7 (ADR-0018). M15 ships @psyuml/interop `toFhir`: a LOSSY, EXPORT-ONLY FHIR R4 document Bundle (Composition + ClinicalImpression + Observation, + CarePlan/Goal, + FamilyMemberHistory/List for relational diagrams) with a structured `loss` report (the §7 'limits MUST be documented' made executable) + `validateFhirBundle` (a zod SUBSET check + reference integrity, NOT a full FHIR validator). Non-diagnostic (Observation, never Condition — §A.3); de-identified + audience-scoped by default (reuses @psyuml/privacy, REQ-PRIVACY). NO importer / round-trip — the diagram stays source-of-truth. Surfaced as `psyuml export`. Still to come: SNOMED/LOINC terminology binding (text CodeableConcepts only today).

requirements.title: Evaluation suite (comprehension, collaborative validity, editability, fidelity, safety, privacy, interop, accessibility)
requirements.notes: The evaluation SUITE is built: Tier-A automation runs and is green (conformance + validate + privacy gates), and the Tier-B instruments are written (docs/adoption/comprehension-instruments.md, proposed/unvalidated). The ONLY remaining work is RUNNING the Tier-B human studies with real participants — layperson comprehension, inter-rater reliability, multi-school (Delphi) endorsement — which by definition cannot be satisfied in-repo. This requirement is the honest home of that owed evidence and the Stage-4 v1.0 gate; PsyUML stays v0.x until those studies are run. It is deliberately NOT marked implemented.

requirements.title: Notation style guide + clinician/client cheat-sheets
requirements.notes: Alt-plan cross-check (idea-incorporation §7). All three named deliverables shipped: docs/format-reference.md (field-level authoring reference + per-diagram quick-guide + validation rules), docs/cheatsheets.md (one-page clinician + plain-language client quick references), and docs/style-guide.md (the visual notation style guide — glyph forms, colour-redundant/line-weight semantics, epistemic/consolidation/valence/band encoding, layout conventions, ritual cultural-sensitivity, cross-school provenance). Printable blank session templates are tracked separately (REQ-TEMPLATES).

requirements.title: Printable blank session templates
requirements.notes: Alt-plan cross-check: hand-drawable blank templates per diagram type for paper use in session. render.blankTemplate(model) keeps a diagram's structure (bands, positions, node kinds, edges) but replaces node labels with per-kind fill-in prompts and clears edge labels/triggers, keeping the disclaimer + crisis line on the print. Exposed as `psyuml template <file> [-o out.svg]` — generate a blank scaffold for ANY of the 12 diagram types from its seed. Could add ready-made template SVGs to the repo later, but the generator is the deliverable.

requirements.title: Multi-school worked-case corpus
requirements.notes: Alt-plan cross-check: worked teaching cases beyond the composite 'R.', each a clearly-fictional non-pathologising composite with dual clinician/client labels, the right safety fields, and a pinned golden SVG. Added: social-anxiety-loop.psyuml (process-loop, 'T.') — a post-event rumination/'post-mortem' loop with a reinforcing cycle (avoidance prevents disconfirmation) and an early exit, distinct from the existing panic loop; perfectionism-parts.psyuml (parts-map, 'M.') — perfectionist driver vs. procrastinator with an inner critic carrying TWO opposed origin-claims (IFS+schema) to exercise the contested-origin rendering (provenance.node-mixed-school) plus a manager↔firefighter conflict and a dissociative barrier; family-genogram.psyuml (relational-field, 'K.') — a three-generation genogram on the McGoldrick glyph set (male/female/index person, plus a faith-community system) wired with conflict/fused/distant/cutoff/close ties. Each is auto-included in the examples-corpus lint (validate, both layers), the conformance suite (round-trip + accessible SVG + monochrome), and a render golden test. Further cases (grief-ritual, CBT panic for a new person, ...) can follow under the same wiring.

requirements.title: Practitioner handbook / tutorial
requirements.notes: docs/handbook.md ships the practitioner tutorial: five working principles (the §L.2/§A.3 commitments, most validator-enforced), the clinician/client layers, a 'choosing a diagram' guide, per-diagram how-tos for all 12 types (when/build/in-session/pitfall + a shipped example each, with real validator rule names), co-creating-in-session workflow (start from the client's words, draw together, mark uncertainty, progressive reveal, snapshot/compare, redact before sharing), cross-school honesty (vocabulary swap + contested-origin provenance), safety/ethics in practice (the export gates + clinician duties incl. a real local crisis contact per ADR-0008), exercises/self-guided reflection (with crisis caveat), and §9 against pseudo-clinical overreach (unvalidated v0.x; design arguments not trials; ritual evidence bounded; translations are approximations). Complements rather than duplicates cheatsheets/format-reference/style-guide/extension-guide. Deferred (enhancements beyond this requirement, not blockers): in-session video/worked walkthroughs and the workshop/facilitator material (REQ-ADOPTION).

requirements.title: Adoption pack (workshops, extension guide, comprehension instruments)
requirements.notes: Adoption pack under docs/adoption/, three parts: (1) workshop.md — a runnable ~3h introductory clinician workshop + facilitator script (learning objectives, timed agenda, hands-on State-Map/loop-with-exit/Resource-map exercises, talking points, a safety/ethics segment, deck outline, feedback form) that teaches FROM the handbook + cheatsheets + examples; (2) extension-contributor-guide.md — the clinician PROCESS for proposing a new symbol/stereotype/profile (satisfy the four §K rules, draft an ExtensionProfile, validate with `psyuml lint-profile`, attach rationale/evidence, submit, review, semver), wrapping the §K mechanics in docs/extension-guide.md (REQ-EXTENSION-MECH); (3) comprehension-instruments.md — PROPOSED, UNVALIDATED Tier-B instruments (layperson crisis-chart/State-Map comprehension test with sample items + scoring, inter-rater formulation-reliability task, multi-school Delphi consensus sketch) + a pilot-study design with go/no-go thresholds tied to the Stage-4 gate. The instruments are proposed/unvalidated and administering them does NOT constitute evidence; the pack EXTENDS REQ-EVAL-SUITE (operationalizes its Tier B). Honest framing throughout: unvalidated v0.x, supervised pilot use, §L.2 (support-not-replace, non-pathologising, consent + secular default, no overreach).

requirements.title: v0.2: diagram families taxonomy (group the diagram types by the question they answer)
requirements.notes: v0.2 (ADR-0014) groups the 12 v0.1 diagram TYPES into 8 cognitive FAMILIES (the question each answers): Field / Cycle / Parts / Pattern / Journey / Change / Ritual / Composite. @psyuml/profiles ships FAMILIES (descriptors) + FAMILY_OF (every DiagramType → exactly one family) + familyOf()/listFamilies()/diagramsInFamily(); metadata over the existing model (no schema break). Pattern is realized today via the process-loop renderer (the cat-sdr example) and Composite (multi-view board) is future — both are defined in the taxonomy but have no dedicated type yet. Still to come: the editor groups its diagram picker by family (M13).

requirements.title: v0.2: audience profiles (clinician / client / picture) — same semantics, different visual compression
requirements.notes: v0.2 (ADR-0014/0016, spec §2) defines three audience profiles sharing identical semantics but different visual compression: clinician (full relations + interpretation + provenance/confidence), client (plain language, capped symbols, actionable foreground), and picture (low-literacy/child; pictographic; picture symbols MUST pass the §5 comprehension gate before they are frozen). M11: @psyuml/profiles ships AUDIENCE_PROFILES + audienceProfile() + withinSymbolBudget(). M13 (ADR-0016): @psyuml/render gains the single render() dispatcher that resolves audience -> label layer + showInterpretive (clinician shows the analytic surface; client/picture hide the contested/as-if/confidence + cross-school provenance, keeping the structural loop, topology, exits, and the honest dashed border); the editor groups its diagram picker by family + offers the audience selector + a symbol-budget nudge. Profiles MUST NOT change the model, only rendering (proven by a render-does-not-mutate test); explicit layer/showInterpretive still win, so goldens + the CLI are unchanged. Still to come: picture-profile pictographic symbols via the M14 comprehension gate.

requirements.title: v0.2: notation comprehension testing as a release gate (participatory design + ISO 9186)
requirements.notes: Deep research (v0.2-research-synthesis §4) strongly supports comprehension-testing symbols with laypeople BEFORE freezing the asset library, and a validated method exists. v0.2 spec §5 adopts a two-tier gate. M14 (ADR-0017) ships the half that can be built honestly: (Tier-A, in CI) `@psyuml/profiles` NOTATION_SYMBOLS enumerates the symbol set under test and `auditNotation()` enforces discriminability (no shared glyph) + dual-coding of safety-critical symbols (a redundant word, never glyph/colour-alone) + a gloss/unique-id per symbol; (Tier-B protocol, docs) comprehension-instruments.md gains Instrument D (ISO 9186 per-symbol, >=67% general / >=85% safety, wrong/opposite-meaning reported, participatory generation first) + a per-symbol ledger whose every Tier-B cell is PENDING. Tier-B needs real participants and is NOT done — it remains the v0.x->v1.0 gate; results MUST NOT be fabricated (an LLM dry-run is not a sample). Status stays in-progress until the human studies run.

requirements.title: v0.2: CAT-derived Pattern semantics — loop topologies (trap/dilemma/snag) + exits, ontology-neutral
requirements.notes: v0.2 (ADR-0014/0015, spec §4) lifts CAT's SDR machinery school-agnostically: `Edge.loopTopology` names the maintaining-loop SHAPE — trap (self-confirming), dilemma (false-binary fork), snag (self-truncating) — and renderLoopMap draws a centre marker (distinct monochrome glyph + a redundant uppercase word, never colour/glyph alone) plus alt-text gloss. `exit` stays the canonical intervention marker and the path-of-hope rule (≥1 exit/resource/self) is retained in @psyuml/validate. Internal nodes are ontology-neutral: `Properties.asIf` flags an as-if/metaphor framing so the model never bakes in one metaphysics of mind (reciprocal-role / observing-eye remain optional CAT-dialect tags). All additive/backward-compatible — a plain v0.1 loop renders byte-identically (process-loop.svg unchanged). Still to come: per-topology participatory + comprehension-tested glyphs (M14); editor authoring of topology/as-if (M13).

requirements.title: v0.2: provenance + confidence as first-class, orthogonal axes (adds `contested`); interpretive content distinguished
requirements.notes: v0.2 (ADR-0014/0015, spec §3) makes the two orthogonal axes explicit: provenance (where content came from) extends `EpistemicStatus` with `jointly-agreed` / `clinician-inferred` / `contested` (the lived-experience critique that 'jointly-agreed' can mask clinician dominance), and confidence (L/M/H) already exists. `INTERPRETIVE_STATUSES` + `isInterpretive()` are the single shared predicate so renderers and lints agree on descriptive-vs-interpretive; renderLoopMap draws interpretive content DASHED (descriptive solid — the v0.1 convention), surfaces a `contested` ⚖ marker + as-if qualifier on the node label, and echoes contested/interpretive standing AND confidence into alt-text (never on border/colour alone). Subsumes/aligns with v0.1 epistemicStatus; additive + round-trip-safe. The exact 5-value scheme is a design-inference (see synthesis §3).

requirements.title: v0.2: the Composite family — one case across several views, cross-navigated by shared ids
requirements.notes: v0.2 (ADR-0019, spec §2) gives the Composite family — previously taxonomy-only — real output. `renderComposite(models, options)` arranges several member views of ONE case as titled panels (each rendered through the `render()` dispatcher, so the audience profile applies, and nested as a scaled sub-svg) over a `sharedNodeIds()` index — the node ids present in >=2 views (spec §H.10 cross-diagram threads), tagged `data-shared-id`/`data-composite-panel` for cross-navigation. Takes an ARRAY of existing models (a case file), NOT a new model-schema type — additive, no Tier-1 / schema change, never mutates a member. Known nit: nested member svgs duplicate the `arrow` marker def (harmless; ADR-0019). Editor composite UI is future.

requirements.title: v0.2: cultural-permission flag on §K symbols (closed/restricted traditions MUST declare permission)
requirements.notes: v0.2 (ADR-0019, spec §6) adds a `cultural` block to `StereotypeDef` (tradition / restricted / permission / attribution) and a `validateProfile` rule: a `restricted` symbol with no `permission` is a `profile.cultural-permission` ERROR; with permission it surfaces a `profile.cultural-restricted` INFO ('not a generic reusable icon'). Enforced by `psyuml lint-profile` (no CLI change). A worked `CULTURAL_PACK_EXAMPLE` ships as the template (the tradition is an illustrative placeholder; a real pack names its source + authorization). This is a DECLARATION check (permission stated), not verification that permission was granted — it makes the §6 obligation explicit + auditable. Extends REQ-EXTENSION-MECH; additive (the field is optional).
